definition_zh: 平底锅；锅；盘子；用于构成复合词表示器具
definition_en: a wide, shallow metal container with a handle, used for cooking food
core_image: 一柄宽扁的铁盘，架在火上把食物摊平煎熟
scene: 周末清晨的厨房里飘着香气，妈妈在灶前忙碌。She cracked two eggs into a hot pan and listened to them sizzle.
sceneCN: 这里 pan 是「平底锅」（第 1 个义项：烹调用的宽浅金属容器）；句意是她把两个鸡蛋磕进热平底锅里，听着滋滋作响。

pos.zh: 用平底锅烹调；（在淘金盘中）淘洗

collocations.phrase: bake the cake in a pan
clean the pan with a sponge

derivatives.zh: 由 sauce（调味汁）加 pan 构成，义为「炖锅；深平底锅」
由 fry（煎炸）加 pan 构成，义为「煎锅」
由 pan 加 cake 构成，义为「薄煎饼」，因在平锅中摊开煎制而得名

senses.title: A shallow cooking vessel
senses.definition: a wide, shallow metal container with a long handle, used for frying or cooking
senses.definitionCN: 带长柄的宽浅金属容器，用来煎炸或烹煮食物
senses.example: Heat the oil in a large pan before adding the onions.
senses.exampleCN: 先把油倒进大平底锅烧热，再放洋葱。
senses.why: The core image is a flat metal dish over fire; everyday cooking made this the most basic sense.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是架在火上的宽浅金属盘，日常烹调使它成为最基础的义项。

senses.title: A similar container of any kind
senses.definition: any similar open container, such as a dish used for baking or measuring
senses.definitionCN: 任何类似的敞口容器，如用于烘烤或称量的盘皿
senses.example: Press the dough evenly across the baking pan.
senses.exampleCN: 把面团均匀地压进烤盘里。
senses.why: The flat, open shape extends from cooking pots to any wide dish that holds things.
senses.whyCN: 宽扁敞口的形状从烹调锅具延伸到任何盛放东西的宽浅盘皿。

senses.title: To pan for gold
senses.definition: to wash gravel in a pan in order to find gold or other minerals
senses.definitionCN: 把砂砾放进淘盘中用水洗涤，以寻找金子等矿物
senses.example: Many prospectors panned the rivers of California in the gold rush.
senses.exampleCN: 淘金潮中许多探矿者在加利福尼亚的河流里淘洗砂金。
senses.why: The pan is both the tool and the action of swirling it to separate gold from gravel.
senses.whyCN: 淘盘既是工具，也指摇动淘盘把金子从砂砾中分离出来的动作。

senses.title: To criticize harshly
senses.definition: to criticize a film, book, or performance very severely
senses.definitionCN: 对电影、书籍或演出进行非常严厉的批评
senses.example: Critics panned the film for its weak plot.
senses.exampleCN: 影评人猛烈批评这部电影情节薄弱。
senses.why: This sense extends the idea of "flattening" something under a blow, like pounding it flat in a pan.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项把「拍扁打平」的画面延伸开来，像在锅里把东西压平一样把作品贬得一无是处。

senses.title: A wide natural hollow
senses.definition: a wide, shallow natural hollow in the ground, especially one that holds water or salt
senses.definitionCN: 地面上宽而浅的自然洼地，尤指存水或存盐的地方
senses.example: Salt is collected from the shallow pans along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 盐从沿海的浅盐滩中采集而来。
senses.why: The shallow, basin-like shape of the pan is applied to flat natural depressions.
senses.whyCN: 浅盆般的形状被借用来指平坦的天然洼陷地形。

intro.en: Pan is one of the oldest household words in English, tracing back to a common Germanic word for a flat vessel.
intro.cn: pan 是英语中最古老的家用词之一，可追溯到日耳曼语族中表示扁平器皿的同一词源。

items.en: panne meant a pan or a flat vessel for cooking.
items.cn: 古英语 panne 意为平底锅或烹调用的扁平器皿。

items.en: The word comes from a common Germanic root *panno, meaning a flat vessel.
items.cn: 该词来自日耳曼语共同词根 *panno，意为扁平器皿（重构形式）。

items.en: Old Norse panna is a close cognate, suggesting a shared northern European borrowing.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 panna 是密切的同源词，表明这是北欧的共同借词或共同遗产。

items.en: It is generally held to be related to Latin patina, a broad shallow dish, which itself came from Greek.
items.cn: 一般认为它与拉丁语 patina（宽浅盘皿）相关，而 patina 又源自希腊语。

items.en: The word stayed in continuous use for cooking vessels across the medieval period.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，该词持续用于指称烹调器皿。

items.en: Compound words such as frying pan and saucepan, and verbs like pan for gold, developed in the modern period.
items.cn: 现代英语发展出 frying pan、saucepan 等复合词，以及 pan for gold 这类动词用法。

note.en: Pan sits in a family of everyday vessels and compounds; the words below are easily confused or closely related.
note.cn: pan 处于日常器皿词与复合词家族中，下列词容易混淆或关系密切。

entries.definition: a deep round container for cooking, deeper than a pan
entries.definitionCN: 深圆烹调容器，比 pan 深；两者同属炊具但形状不同

entries.definition: a deep pan with a handle, used for sauces and boiling
entries.definitionCN: 有柄的深锅，用于煮酱汁；由 sauce 加 pan 构成

entries.definition: a flat pan with a long handle for frying food
entries.definitionCN: 长柄平底的煎锅；pan 的最常见复合词

entries.definition: a thin pointed piece of metal, only one letter away from pan
entries.definitionCN: 大头针；与 pan 仅一字母之差，拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: a shallow container for serving or baking food
entries.definitionCN: 浅口盛器，用于上菜或烘烤；与 pan 的器皿义相邻

entries.definition: a flat board or shallow container for carrying things
entries.definitionCN: 托盘；形状同为宽浅，但通常不带柄不直接加热

entries.definition: a deep round-bottomed Chinese cooking pan
entries.definitionCN: 中式圆底炒锅；同为烹调锅具，形制不同

entries.definition: a container with a lid and spout, used for boiling water
entries.definitionCN: 水壶；同为厨房金属器具，专用于烧水

normalIntro.en: Use the root shape and real compounds to fix the word in memory.
normalIntro.cn: 利用形状意象和真实复合词来锁定这个词。

normal.en: Pan sounds like the Chinese word "pen" (pen2), which also means a wide, shallow container.
normal.cn: pan 的发音与中文「盆（pén）」相近，两者都是宽浅容器，音义双关便于记忆。

normal.en: frying pan = fry + pan, the pan you fry things in.
normal.cn: frying pan 即「煎锅」，由 fry 加 pan 构成，记复合词顺带记住本词。

normal.en: saucepan = sauce + pan, a deeper pan for sauces.
normal.cn: saucepan 即「炖锅」，由 sauce 加 pan 构成，与煎锅形成深浅对照。

normal.en: pancake = pan + cake, a cake cooked flat in a pan.
normal.cn: pancake 即「薄煎饼」，pan 加 cake，锅煎的饼。

normal.en: pan for gold: swirl the pan, the gold stays, the gravel washes away.
normal.cn: pan for gold 淘金：摇动淘盘，金子留下，砂砾被水冲走。

abstract.en: Picture a flat iron disc with a long handle glowing over the fire.
abstract.cn: 想象一只带长柄的扁铁盘在火上发亮，这就是 pan 的核心画面。

abstract.en: Critics pan a movie: they flatten it like a pancake.
abstract.cn: 影评人 pan 一部电影：像摊煎饼一样把它压扁贬低。

abstract.en: A salt pan in the desert: a shallow basin where water evaporates.
abstract.cn: 沙漠中的盐沼：浅浅的盆状洼地，水分蒸发后留下盐。

examples.en: She cracked two eggs into a hot pan and listened to them sizzle.
examples.cn: 她把两个鸡蛋磕进热平底锅里，听着滋滋作响。

examples.en: Gold prospectors panned the river in search of a fortune.
examples.cn: 淘金者在河里淘洗砂砾，希望寻得财富。

examples.en: Critics panned the play, but audiences loved it.
examples.cn: 评论家对这部戏大加批评，观众却很喜欢。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「盘」——pan 谐音「盘」，平底锅正是一只浅浅的盘子架在火上；淘金的人端着「盘」在水里摇，影评人把烂片「盘」得体无完肤。

root: pan 来自古英语 panne，可追溯至日耳曼共同词根 *panno（重构形式），一般认为与拉丁语 patina（宽浅盘皿）相关，而 patina 源自希腊语；属于英语中存续最久的器皿词之一。

sensesIntro.en: From the basic cooking vessel, pan spreads to any wide shallow container, then to the verb of panning for gold, the critical sense of panning a film, and flat natural basins.
sensesIntro.cn: 从基本的烹调用具出发，pan 先扩展到各类宽浅盘皿，再延伸为淘金动词、影评论动词，以及盆状地形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wide, shallow handled vessel over fire
core.cn: 核心意象：架在火上的宽浅带柄盘皿

branches.en: The basic frying vessel
branches.cn: 基本的煎炒锅具

branches.en: Any wide open container for holding things
branches.cn: 各类宽浅敞口容器

branches.en: Swirling gravel in the pan to wash out gold
branches.cn: 摇盘淘洗砂金

branches.en: Flattening a work by harsh criticism
branches.cn: 以严厉批评把作品压扁

branches.en: Shallow basin-shaped hollows in the land
branches.cn: 盆状的天然浅洼地

intro.en: Pan rarely stands alone in formation; it is best learned through its compounds and set phrases.
intro.cn: pan 很少单独参与构词，最有效的学习途径是它的复合词与固定短语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin cognate patina gave English panning-like dish words and the colour word patina.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词 patina 派生出英语中与盘皿相关的词，还有表示「铜绿；光润表面」的 patina。

items.example: Heat the frying pan until it smokes lightly.
items.exampleCN: 把煎锅加热到微微冒烟。

items.example: Boil the pasta in a large saucepan.

items.meaning: a flat cake fried in a pan
items.example: We ate pancakes with maple syrup for breakfast.
items.exampleCN: 早餐我们吃了配枫糖浆的薄煎饼。

items.meaning: to turn out well; to succeed
items.example: The investment did not pan out in the end.
items.exampleCN: 这项投资最终没有成功。

items.meaning: to wash gravel for gold in a pan
items.example: Tourists still pan for gold in those streams.
items.exampleCN: 游客们仍在那些溪流里淘金。

items.meaning: a metal pan for holding burning fuel
items.example: The camper set the fire pan on stones.
items.exampleCN: 露营者把火盆放在石头上。

items.meaning: a pan used in an oven
items.example: Grease the baking pan before pouring in the batter.
items.exampleCN: 倒入面糊前先给烤盘抹油。

items.meaning: a shallow basin where salt is harvested
items.example: Workers walked across the salt pan at dawn.

items.meaning: a surface film; a superficial polish
items.example: The bronze statue has a green patina.
items.exampleCN: 青铜雕像上覆着绿色铜绿。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 宽浅盘皿；一般认为与 pan 同源

definition_zh: 纸；报纸；论文；试卷；文件；纸做的
definition_en: the thin material used for writing and printing, a newspaper, a written study or examination, official documents, and made of paper
core_image: 台灯下一叠白纸，边角被翻得起了毛
scene: 书桌的台灯下，一叠稿纸被翻得起了毛边，最上面那张只写了一个标题。He pushed the paper aside and started again on a clean sheet.
sceneCN: 这里 paper 是「纸」（第 1 个义项：用来书写印刷的薄材料）；句意为他把那张纸推到一边，重新拿一张干净的纸从头写起。图中可辨识物件：台灯、起毛的稿纸、只写了标题的一页。

pos.zh: 纸做的；纸上的；名义上的

derivatives.zh: paper 加 -y 构成，指像纸一样薄而脆的
paper 与 work 复合而成，指文书工作
news 与 paper 复合而成，指报纸
paper 与 back 复合而成，指纸面平装书

senses.title: The material used for writing
senses.definition: the thin material made from wood pulp or other fibres, used for writing, printing and wrapping
senses.definitionCN: 用木浆或其他纤维制成的薄材料，用于书写、印刷和包装
senses.example: He pushed the paper aside and started again on a clean sheet.
senses.exampleCN: 他把那张纸推到一边，重新拿一张干净的纸从头写起。
senses.why: The word began as papyrus, the Egyptian reed pressed into sheets, so the material itself is the oldest and most literal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是 papyrus，即埃及的那种芦苇，压成薄片用来书写，所以「材料」本身就是最古老、最字面的义项。

senses.title: A newspaper
senses.definition: a set of printed sheets published daily or weekly with news and comment
senses.definitionCN: 每日或每周出版、刊载新闻与评论的一套印刷纸张
senses.example: She reads the paper on the train every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天早上在火车上看报纸。
senses.why: A newspaper is literally paper that carries news, so English kept the material's name for the daily object and dropped the first half of the compound.
senses.whyCN: 报纸字面上就是「载着新闻的纸」，英语把这个日刊直接叫作纸，省掉了复合词的前一半。

senses.title: A written study or an exam
senses.definition: a piece of academic writing on one topic, or the set of questions used in an examination
senses.definitionCN: 就一个题目写成的学术文章，或考试所用的一整套题目
senses.example: He published a paper on coastal erosion last year.
senses.exampleCN: 他去年发表了一篇关于海岸侵蚀的论文。
senses.why: A paper is a piece of writing that exists on paper; scholars hand in such sheets and examiners set them, so the same word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 论文就是写在纸上的一份文字；学者交上这样的纸页，出题人发出的也是这样的纸页，同一个词就同时覆盖了两边。

senses.title: Official documents
senses.definition: papers, the documents that prove who you are or what you are allowed to do
senses.definitionCN: 复数形式 papers，指证明身份或获准做某事的文件
senses.example: The guard asked to see her papers at the border.
senses.exampleCN: 边检人员要求看她的证件。
senses.why: Identity and permission are proved by printed sheets, so the plural papers came to mean the documents a person must carry.
senses.whyCN: 身份与许可都靠印好的纸页来证明，于是复数 papers 就指一个人必须随身携带的那些文件。

senses.title: Made of paper; existing only on paper
senses.titleCN: 纸做的；只停留在纸面上的
senses.definition: made of paper, or true only in written records and not in real life
senses.definitionCN: 用纸做的；或只在书面记录中成立、在现实中并不成立
senses.example: They handed out paper cups at the entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在入口处发放纸杯。
senses.why: When something exists only as figures on a sheet, it is paper in the adjective's sense: it looks solid but has no body behind it.
senses.whyCN: 当某样东西只以纸上的数字存在时，它就是这个形容词意义上的 paper：看上去实在，背后却没有实体。

intro.en: Paper is named after papyrus, the reed of the Nile; Greek papuros passed into Latin as papyrus and into English through Old French papier.
intro.cn: paper 得名于尼罗河的纸莎草；希腊语 papuros 进入拉丁语作 papyrus，又经古法语 papier 进入英语。

items.en: Papuros was the Egyptian reed whose pith was pressed into writing sheets, and Greek used the same word for the sheets.
items.cn: papuros 是埃及的芦苇，其茎髓被压成书写用的薄片，希腊语也用同一个词指这些薄片。

items.en: Latin took papyrus from Greek for both the plant and the writing material sold across the empire.
items.cn: 拉丁语从希腊语借来 papyrus，同时指这种植物和在帝国各地出售的书写材料。

items.en: Old French papier named the material, and Norman scribes brought the word to England.
items.cn: 古法语 papier 指这种材料，诺曼抄写员把这个词带到了英格兰。

items.en: Middle English paper covered the sheets and, as printing spread, the newspaper and the written study.
items.cn: 中古英语的 paper 指纸页，随着印刷术传播，也指报纸与写成的研究。

items.en: Modern English keeps papers for documents and adds paper as an adjective for anything that exists only on a page.
items.cn: 现代英语用 papers 指文件，并把 paper 用作形容词，指只存在于纸面上的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the reed, the material and the things made from it; the near-meaning group gathers other words for sheets and written records.
note.cn: 形近组沿芦苇、材料以及用它做成的东西展开；近义组收其他表示纸页与书面记录的词。

entries.definition: The ancient writing material made from pressed reed, which gave paper its name.
entries.definitionCN: 用压制芦苇制成的古代书写材料，正是 paper 得名的来源。

entries.definition: Thin, dry and light, like paper.
entries.definitionCN: 薄、干、轻，像纸一样。

entries.definition: A printed publication of news, literally news on paper.
entries.definitionCN: 刊载新闻的印刷出版物，字面就是印在纸上的新闻。

entries.definition: A book with a thin flexible cover rather than a hard one.
entries.definitionCN: 用薄软封面而非硬壳装订的书。

entries.definition: A single flat piece of paper, cloth or other thin material.
entries.definitionCN: 纸、布等薄材料的单张平面。

entries.definition: An official record of information, now often kept as a computer file.
entries.definitionCN: 信息的正式记录，如今常以电子文件形式保存。

entries.definition: A periodical publishing scholarly articles in a field.
entries.definitionCN: 在某一领域刊载学术文章的期刊。

normalIntro.en: The word began as the name of a reed, survived as the name of the sheet, and then lent itself to everything printed on that sheet.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初是一种芦苇的名字，后来成为纸页的名字，再借给写在纸页上的一切。

normal.en: Papyrus was a Nile reed, and paper keeps its name even after the reed was replaced by rags and wood pulp.
normal.cn: papyrus 是一种尼罗河芦苇，即使原料早已换成破布与木浆，paper 仍留着它的名字。

normal.en: A newspaper is literally paper that carries news, which is why the material's name survived in the daily.
normal.cn: 报纸字面上就是载着新闻的纸，所以「材料」的名字留在了这份日刊里。

normal.en: Papers in the plural means documents, the sheets you must show at a border.
normal.cn: 复数 papers 指文件，也就是在边境必须拿出来给人看的那几张纸。

normal.en: A paper can be a study you publish, because scholarship once travelled as printed sheets.
normal.cn: paper 也可以指你发表的论文，因为学问曾经就靠印好的纸页传播。

normal.en: On paper marks a plan that has not yet met the world.
normal.cn: on paper 标出一个还没和现实碰面的计划。

abstract.en: Paper is a surface that holds a thought longer than a voice can.
abstract.cn: 纸是一种表面，能让一个想法留存得比声音更久。

abstract.en: A sheet is cheap, which is why it can carry both a shopping list and a treaty.
abstract.cn: 一张纸很便宜，所以它既能承载购物清单，也能承载条约。

abstract.en: To say something is only on paper is to doubt whether the page can change anything.
abstract.cn: 说某件事只停留在纸面上，就是在怀疑这页纸能否改变任何东西。

examples.en: He pushed the paper aside and started again on a clean sheet.
examples.cn: 他把那张纸推到一边，重新拿一张干净的纸从头写起。

examples.en: He published a paper on coastal erosion last year.
examples.cn: 他去年发表了一篇关于海岸侵蚀的论文。

examples.en: The deal looked good on paper but failed in practice.
examples.cn: 这笔交易在纸面上看着不错，实际操作却失败了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佩珀」——像胡椒一样又薄又轻的一张，一吹就飘走；记住 paper 是纸。

root: 希腊语 papuros（纸莎草）— 拉丁语 papyrus — 古法语 papier — 英语 paper。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the sheet you can write on; the senses then move to the daily printed sheet, the study written on it, the documents you carry, and finally the adjective for what exists only there.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是可以书写的纸页；义项随后转到每日印出的那张纸、写在上面的研究、随身携带的文件，最后是「只存在于纸上」的形容词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of white sheets under a lamp, edges soft from being turned.
core.cn: 核心意象：台灯下一叠白纸，边角因反复翻动而发毛。

branches.en: a blank sheet waiting under a lamp
branches.cn: 台灯下等着的空白纸

definition_zh: 原谅；饶恕；赦免；（礼貌用语）请再说一遍
definition_en: to forgive someone or officially free them from punishment; a polite word asking someone to repeat
core_image: 松开惩罚的手：本要落下的责罚被收了回去
scene: 听到同桌小声嘀咕了一句没听清，他放下了手中的笔。"Pardon? Could you say that again?" he asked politely.
sceneCN: 这里 pardon 是「（礼貌地）请再说一遍」（第 4 个义项）；句意是他没听清，礼貌地请对方重复一遍。

senses.title: To forgive an offence
senses.definition: to forgive someone for a fault or wrong they have done
senses.definitionCN: 原谅某人所犯的过失或错误
senses.example: He begged her pardon for arriving so late.
senses.exampleCN: 他为自己迟到这么久请求她的原谅。
senses.why: The core image is withdrawing the hand of punishment; forgiving means pulling back the penalty.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是收回惩罚之手；原谅就是把将要落下的责罚收回去。

senses.title: To officially free from legal punishment
senses.definition: to officially allow someone who has been convicted of a crime to go free or be released from punishment
senses.definitionCN: 官方正式免除被定罪者的刑罚或准予其免受处罚
senses.example: The governor granted a full pardon to the wrongly convicted man.
senses.exampleCN: 州长对蒙冤定罪的男子颁布了完全赦免。
senses.why: The legal sense keeps the same image: the state withdraws a punishment already decided.
senses.whyCN: 法律义项保留同一画面：国家收回已经判定的惩罚。

senses.title: A polite way to say sorry
senses.titleCN: 抱歉；（引起注意或致歉的礼貌语）
senses.definition: a polite expression used to say sorry or to get someone's attention
senses.definitionCN: 表示歉意或引起对方注意的礼貌用语
senses.example: "Pardon me," he said, as he squeezed past the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 「借过一下，」他说着挤过人群。
senses.why: Asking pardon literally means asking to be forgiven for a small disturbance.
senses.whyCN: 说 pardon me 字面上就是请求对方原谅自己小小的打扰。

senses.title: A polite request to repeat
senses.definition: a polite question asking someone to repeat what they said, often because you did not hear it
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌地请对方重复刚才的话，常因没听清
senses.example: "Pardon? I didn't catch your name," she said.
senses.exampleCN: 「您再说一遍好吗？我没听清您的名字，」她说。
senses.why: In British English, rising pardon politely asks the speaker to try again.
senses.whyCN: 在英式英语中，语调上扬的 pardon 礼貌地请对方再说一次。

intro.en: Pardon travelled from Latin through Old French into English, always built on the idea of giving completely and fairly.
intro.cn: pardon 经拉丁语与古法语进入英语，词义始终建立在「完全而公正地给予」这一根义之上。

items.en: The root is perdonare: per- (completely, thoroughly) plus donare (to give), literally "to give wholeheartedly".
items.cn: 词根是拉丁语 perdonare：per-（完全地）加 donare（给予），字面义为「全心全意地给予」。

items.en: Old French pardonner meant to grant, to forgive, and to remit a punishment.
items.cn: 古法语 pardonner 意为给予、宽恕、免除惩罚。

items.en: In medieval church use, perdonare and related forms covered the remission of sins and penalties.
items.cn: 在中世纪教会语境中，perdonare 及相关形式用于表示赦罪与减免惩罚。

items.en: Modern French keeps pardon as both the forgiveness noun and the everyday "sorry" expression.
items.cn: 现代法语中 pardon 既是「宽恕」名词，也是日常表示「抱歉」的用语。

items.en: English took the word from Old French in the 13th century, first in the legal and religious senses.
items.cn: 英语于十三世纪从古法语借入该词，最早用于法律与宗教语境。

items.en: Later uses extended it to polite apologies and the request to repeat a sentence.
items.cn: 后来的用法把它扩展为礼貌致歉语和请对方重复的用语。

definition_zh: 伙伴；搭档；合伙人；配偶；与……合伙
definition_en: a person who shares an activity, a business, or a life with another; also to join with someone as a partner
core_image: 两个人各执一端，抬着同一件重物往前走
scene: 双人皮划艇上，前后两人各握一支桨。The two paddlers must keep exactly the same rhythm, because each one is the partner of the other and the boat goes straight only when they pull together.
sceneCN: 这里 partner 是「搭档」（第 2 个义项：并肩干活的搭档）；句意：两名划手必须保持完全一致的节奏，因为彼此是对方的搭档，只有同时划桨船才会走直。图中可辨识物件：双人皮划艇、两支桨、救生衣、水面、同步的桨痕。

senses.title: One who shares a business
senses.titleCN: 共同经营一份生意的人
senses.definition: a person who shares the ownership and risks of a business with one or more others
senses.definitionCN: 与他人共同拥有一家企业并分担风险的人
senses.example: She became a partner in the firm last year.
senses.exampleCN: 她去年成了这家事务所的合伙人。
senses.why: The oldest sense is 'one who shares'. In business the shared thing is ownership itself, so a partner is someone who holds a portion of the firm and is liable for its debts.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是“分享者”。在商业中，被分享的东西就是所有权本身，因此合伙人就是持有企业一份、并对债务负责的人。

senses.title: The one you work beside
senses.definition: a person who works with you on a task, often as an equal
senses.definitionCN: 与你共同完成一项任务的人，通常是平等的一方
senses.example: My lab partner and I split the experiments.
senses.exampleCN: 我和实验搭档分担了实验。
senses.why: Sharing can be sharing work rather than property. Two people each take one end of the task, and equality is built into the word: a partner is not a helper but a counterpart.
senses.whyCN: 分享的对象可以是工作而不是财产。两人各执任务的一端，平等就写在这个词里：partner 不是帮手，而是对等的一方。

senses.title: The one you share a life with
senses.definition: a spouse or a person with whom one lives in a committed romantic relationship
senses.definitionCN: 配偶，或与之处于稳定恋爱关系并共同生活的人
senses.example: He brought his partner to the dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 他带伴侣来参加晚宴。
senses.why: A life is the largest thing two people can share. English extended partner to the domestic sphere in the 18th century, and the word now avoids the assumptions built into husband or wife.
senses.whyCN: 生活是两个人能分享的最大一件事。英语在 18 世纪把 partner 扩展到家庭领域，如今这个词也避开了 husband 或 wife 所带的预设。

senses.title: The one across the table or on the floor
senses.titleCN: 桌对面或舞池里的搭档
senses.definition: the person matched with you in a game, dance, or performance
senses.definitionCN: 在游戏、舞蹈或表演中与你配对的人
senses.example: She danced with a new partner at the competition.
senses.exampleCN: 她在比赛中与一位新舞伴跳舞。
senses.why: A dance or a game assigns roles that only work in pairs. The partner is the other half of a required pair, which is why the word appears wherever a form demands two.
senses.whyCN: 舞蹈或游戏分配的角色只有成对才成立。partner 是某个必需配对中的另一半，因此凡是形式要求两人时，这个词就会出现。

senses.title: Partner in crime: the other half of a secret
senses.definition: a person who joins another in a mischievous or criminal activity, often used humorously
senses.definitionCN: 与他人一起干顽皮或犯罪之事的人，常作幽默用法
senses.example: The two children were partners in crime all summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个孩子整个夏天都是“共犯”。
senses.why: The phrase borrows the equality of partnership for something illegal. What is shared is not property but risk and secrecy, and the humorous use keeps the bond while dropping the crime.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把伙伴关系的“平等”借给了非法之事。被分享的不是财产，而是风险与秘密；幽默用法保留了这份联结，却抽掉了犯罪。

senses.title: A partner organisation or country
senses.definition: an organisation, company, or country that cooperates formally with another
senses.definitionCN: 与另一方正式合作的机构、公司或国家
senses.example: The university is a partner in the research consortium.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学是该研究联盟的合作方。
senses.why: Institutions also pair up. Here partnership is a formal relation between entities rather than between persons, but the logic is the same: each brings something and both are bound.
senses.whyCN: 机构也会结对。这里的伙伴关系是实体之间而非人与人之间的正式关系，但逻辑相同：各方都拿出东西，也都受约束。

senses.title: To partner: join as an equal
senses.titleCN: 动词：作为平等一方加入
senses.definition: to join with someone or an organisation as a partner
senses.definitionCN: 作为伙伴与某人或某机构结合
senses.example: The startup partnered with a larger manufacturer.
senses.exampleCN: 这家初创公司与一家更大的制造商结成了伙伴。
senses.why: The verb turns the relation into an act. Partnering is not hiring or assisting; it is the moment two parties agree to stand on the same level, which is why it is popular in business language.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这个关系变成动作。partnering 不是雇佣也不是帮忙，而是两方同意站在同一高度的那一刻，因此它在商业语言里很受欢迎。

senses.title: A partner in a professional firm
senses.definition: a senior member of a law or accounting firm who shares in its ownership and profits
senses.definitionCN: 律师事务所或会计师事务所中持有所有权并分享利润的高级成员
senses.example: Only partners may sign the audit report.
senses.exampleCN: 只有合伙人才能签署审计报告。
senses.why: Professional firms are owned by their senior members, so 'partner' becomes a rank as well as a relation. The title marks both ownership and the right to sign, which is why it is a career goal in law and accounting.
senses.whyCN: 专业事务所由其高级成员拥有，因此 partner 既是关系也是职级。这个头衔同时标记所有权与签署权，所以它成了法律与会计行业的一个职业目标。

intro.en: Partner began as a word for a joint heir and was reshaped by the unrelated word part. The deeper root is Latin pars, but the change from parcener to partner is not fully explained.
intro.cn: partner 最初指共同继承人，后来被另一个词 part 改形。更深词根是拉丁语 pars，但从 parcener 变成 partner 的过程并没有完整解释。

items.en: Partiner is recorded meaning 'partner, sharer'. It is an altered form of parcener 'joint heir, one who shares an inheritance'.
items.cn: partiner 记录于 1300 年前后，意为“伙伴、分享者”。它是 parcener“共同继承人、分得遗产者”的变形。

items.en: Parcener comes from Old French parçonier, from parçon 'division, share', from Latin partitionem 'a dividing', from partire 'to divide', from pars 'part'.
items.cn: parcener 来自古法语 parçonier，再上溯 parçon“分割、一份”，拉丁语 partitionem“划分”，动词 partire“分割”，以及 pars“部分”。

items.en: The -n- of parcener becomes -t-, giving partner. The change is usually attributed to the influence of part, though the exact path is source uncertain.
items.cn: parcener 中的 -n- 变成 -t-，形成 partner。这一变化通常归因于 part 的影响，但确切过程来源不确定。

items.en: The commercial sense 'one who shares in a business' is recorded. The legal and commercial senses grow together, since a partnership is both a relation and a form of ownership.
items.cn: “共同经营生意者”这一商业义记录于 16 世纪 20 年代。法律义与商业义一起成长，因为合伙既是一种关系，也是一种所有权形式。

items.en: The sense 'spouse' is recorded. Modern English extends it to any committed couple and to institutional cooperation: trading partner, partner with.
items.cn: “配偶”义记录于 1749 年。现代英语把它扩展到任何稳定的伴侣关系，也扩展到机构合作：贸易伙伴、与……合作。

note.en: The first group shares the part- root or the -er ending; the second compares words for people joined by work, trust, or love.
note.cn: 第一组共享 part- 词根或 -er 结尾；第二组比较因工作、信任或爱情而结合的人。

entries.definition: concerning only a part; biased in favour of one side. It is an adjective, not a person, and has nothing to do with partnership.
entries.definitionCN: 只涉及一部分的；偏袒一方的。它是形容词，不指人，也与合伙无关。

entries.definition: a division into parts, or a screen that divides a space. It shares the Latin pars root but names a dividing, not a sharing.
entries.definitionCN: 分成若干部分，或隔开空间的屏风。它共享拉丁语 pars 词根，但命名的是“分开”，不是“分享”。

entries.definition: a strong supporter of a party or cause. Its part is a political side, not a share held with another person.
entries.definitionCN: 某一党派或事业的坚定支持者。它的 part 指政治一方，而不是与他人共持的一份。

entries.definition: a very small piece of matter. It is a small part, with the diminutive -cle, and is not a partner.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的物质颗粒。它是“小部分”，带指小后缀 -cle，不是伙伴。

entries.definition: a person you work with, especially in a profession. It is neutral about equality and ownership, while partner implies a share.
entries.definitionCN: 与你共事的人，尤指同一专业。它对平等与所有权保持中性，而 partner 隐含“持有一份”。

entries.definition: a state or person joined with another for mutual support. It is about interests and conflict, while partner can be about work or life.
entries.definitionCN: 为相互支持而结合的国家或个人。它关乎利益与冲突，而 partner 可以关乎工作或生活。

entries.definition: a person who spends time with you. It stresses company, while partner stresses a shared role or share.
entries.definitionCN: 与你共度时光的人。它强调陪伴，而 partner 强调共同的角色或份额。

entries.definition: a husband or wife in law. It is the legal term, while partner is broader and can name an unmarried couple.
entries.definitionCN: 法律上的丈夫或妻子。它是法律术语，而 partner 更宽泛，也可指未婚伴侣。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the sound and the shared load, then three abstract images about equality.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个围绕读音与“共抬一物”的挂钩，再用三个关于“平等”的抽象画面。

normal.en: partner has part inside it: a partner holds a part. The spelling hides the old parcener, but the meaning kept the share.
normal.cn: partner 里面藏着 part：partner 持有一份。拼写掩盖了古老的 parcener，但词义保住了“份额”。

normal.en: Picture two people carrying one heavy box, one at each end. Neither is the boss.
normal.cn: 想两个人抬一个重箱子，各执一端。谁都不是老板。

normal.en: Business partner, dance partner, life partner: the same word slides from money to floor to home.
normal.cn: 商业合伙人、舞伴、人生伴侣：同一个词从钱滑到舞池，再滑到家。

normal.en: partner with, not partner to: the preposition marks standing alongside, not belonging to.
normal.cn: 是 partner with，不是 partner to：介词标记“并肩”，不是“附属”。

normal.en: A law firm promotes you to partner: the title means you now own a piece of the firm.
normal.cn: 律师事务所把你提升为 partner：这个头衔意味着你现在拥有事务所的一份。

abstract.en: A partner is equality made practical: two people who each hold one end and cannot move without the other.
abstract.cn: 伙伴是被实践出来的平等：两人各执一端，缺少对方就无法前进。

abstract.en: Partnership is a share in risk before it is a share in reward; that is why the word fits both marriage and business.
abstract.cn: 合伙先是风险中的一份，然后才是收益中的一份；因此这个词同时适用于婚姻与商业。

abstract.en: Calling someone a partner rather than a helper is a claim about dignity, not about workload.
abstract.cn: 称一个人为 partner 而不是 helper，是在主张尊严，而不是分配工作量。

examples.en: The two firms became partners in a joint venture.
examples.cn: 这两家公司在一次合资中成为合伙人。

examples.en: He partnered with a local charity to rebuild the school.
examples.cn: 他与当地一家慈善机构合作重建了学校。

examples.en: Her partner stayed home while she attended the conference.
examples.cn: 她去开会时，伴侣留在了家里。

dict_mnemonic.note: 把 part 记成“一份”，-ner 记成人：持有一份的人，就是合伙人、搭档、伴侣。
dict_mnemonic.text: part（一份）+ -ner（人）→ 持有一份的人 → 合伙人、搭档、伴侣

root: 古法语 parçonier < parçon“分割、一份” < 拉丁 partitionem / partire < pars“部分”；拼写受 part 影响，由 parcener 变为 partner。

sensesIntro.en: The senses go from shared ownership, to shared work, to a shared life, to a required pair in a game or dance, to a shared secret, to institutional cooperation, to the act of joining, and finally to the rank inside a professional firm.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从共同所有权，转到共担工作、共同生活、游戏或舞蹈中必需的另一半、共同保守的秘密、机构合作、结伴的动作，最后落到专业事务所内部的职级。

core.en: Two people holding one end each of the same load, walking in step
core.cn: 两人各执同一重物的一端，步调一致地前行

branches.en: Ownership: a share in a firm, and the rank that share confers.
branches.cn: 所有权：在企业中的一份，以及这份所有权带来的职级。

branches.en: The required other half: a workmate on a task, and a mate in a dance or game.
branches.cn: 必需的另一半：任务上的同事，以及舞蹈或游戏中的搭档。

branches.en: Intimacy at two temperatures: a life partner and a partner in crime.
branches.cn: 两种温度的亲密：人生伴侣与犯罪同伙。

branches.en: From persons to entities: organisations and countries as partners, still sharing risk.
branches.cn: 从人到实体：机构与国家成为伙伴，仍然共担风险。

branches.en: The verb: to join someone as an equal.
branches.cn: 动词：作为平等一方与某人结合。

intro.en: Partner's family mixes the Latin pars root with native English suffixes: the abstract partnership, the activity, the adjective, and prefixed forms.
intro.cn: partner 的词族把拉丁语 pars 词根与英语本族后缀混在一起：抽象的 partnership、活动名词、形容词，以及加前缀的形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin chain is pars 'part' → partire 'to divide' → partitionem 'a division'. Old French parçon gave parcener, and the spelling later moved toward part.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语链条是 pars“部分”→ partire“分割”→ partitionem“划分”。古法语 parçon 给出 parcener，拼写后来又向 part 靠拢。

items.structure: altered from parcener, influenced by part
items.meaning: one who shares a business, task, or life
items.meaningCN: 共享生意、任务或生活的人
items.example: They have been partners for ten years.
items.exampleCN: 他们做合伙人已经十年。

items.meaning: the relation between partners; a business so owned
items.exampleCN: 这段合伙关系于 2010 年结束。

items.meaning: the act of forming a partnership
items.example: Partnering with local firms cut costs.
items.exampleCN: 与当地公司合作降低了成本。

items.meaning: having a partner; joined in a partnership
items.meaningCN: 有伴侣的；已结成伙伴的
items.example: The survey distinguishes partnered and single adults.
items.exampleCN: 该调查区分有伴侣与单身的成年人。

items.example: Each co-partner holds an equal share.
items.exampleCN: 每位共同合伙人持有相等份额。

items.example: He arrived partnerless at the dinner.
items.exampleCN: 他独自一人来参加晚宴。

items.meaning: a portion or role within a whole
items.meaningCN: 整体中的一份或一个角色
items.example: She played a part in the decision.
items.exampleCN: 她在这个决定中出了一份力。

items.structure: Latin portio, from the pars family
items.example: Each heir received an equal portion.
items.exampleCN: 每位继承人分得相等的一份。

items.meaning: a package; a portion of land
items.example: The land was sold in three parcels.
items.exampleCN: 这块地被分成三份出售。

latinEntries.meaning: a part, a share, a side
latinEntries.example: Pars is the root behind partner and portion.
latinEntries.exampleCN: pars 是 partner 与 portion 背后的词根。

latinEntries.example: Partire gave French partir and English partition.
latinEntries.exampleCN: partire 给出法语 partir 与英语 partition。

latinEntries.example: Partitionem is the source of Old French parçon.
latinEntries.exampleCN: partitionem 是古法语 parçon 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Particella became French parcelle and English parcel.
latinEntries.exampleCN: particella 演变为法语 parcelle 与英语 parcel。

definition_zh: 政党；社交聚会；诉讼或合同的一方；参与人；执行任务的小队；庆祝
definition_en: an organized political group, a social gathering, or one of the sides in a legal or other matter
core_image: 客厅里灯亮到深夜，桌上杯盘未收，同一群人先谈事再举杯，散场时各自站成一伙
scene: 屋顶上串灯亮起来，长桌摆满食物，音乐一响，邻居们陆续上楼。They held a party on the roof to celebrate the new shop.
sceneCN: 屋顶上串灯亮起来，长桌摆满食物，音乐一响，邻居们陆续上楼；句中的这个词指「为庆祝或娱乐把人们请到一起的聚会」（第 2 个义项：围绕一个由头把亲友聚在一处的社交活动）。图中可辨识物件：串灯、长桌、餐盘、音响、楼梯。

pos.zh: 政党；聚会；一方；参与者；小队

党徒；党派的
伙伴；合伙人

senses.title: An organized political group
senses.definition: a lasting organization that contests elections under one name and programme
senses.definitionCN: 以同一个名号与纲领参加选举的持久组织
senses.example: The party won two seats on the city council.
senses.exampleCN: 这个政党在市议会赢下两个席位。
senses.why: The oldest extended sense: one part of the citizen body organizes and speaks for the whole.
senses.whyCN: 这是较早的引申义：公民整体中的一部分组织起来，替整体发言。

senses.title: A social gathering
senses.definition: an occasion when people are invited to eat, drink and enjoy themselves together
senses.definitionCN: 邀请人们聚在一起吃喝、娱乐的场合
senses.example: She invited forty guests to the party.
senses.exampleCN: 她请了四十位客人参加聚会。
senses.why: A party is a group of people assembled on purpose; the pleasure is added to the gathering, not to the word's core.
senses.whyCN: 聚会就是一群人特意聚到一起；欢乐是加在「聚」之上的，而不是这个词的核心。

senses.title: One side in a legal matter
senses.definition: one of the persons or groups bound by a contract, a lawsuit or a treaty
senses.definitionCN: 受合同、诉讼或条约约束的一个人或一方
senses.example: Each party must sign every page of the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 合同每一页都必须由各方签字。
senses.why: Law divides a matter into sides, and each side is a part with rights and duties.
senses.whyCN: 法律把一件事分成若干方，每一方都是带着权利与义务的「一部分」。

senses.title: A participant in an activity
senses.definition: a person or group that takes part in a discussion, an agreement or an event
senses.definitionCN: 参加讨论、协议或事件的人或团体
senses.example: All parties to the talks agreed on the timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 会谈各方就时间表达成一致。
senses.why: To be a party is to hold a part: the participant is one of the pieces that make the event happen.
senses.whyCN: 成为一方就是持有一份：参与人是促成这件事的若干块之一。

senses.title: A small task team
senses.definition: a small group sent out to do one job, such as a search or a survey
senses.definitionCN: 为完成某一任务而派出的小队，如搜索队或勘察队
senses.example: A search party set out before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 一支搜索队在天亮前出发。
senses.why: The group is a part detached from a larger body and given a single errand.
senses.whyCN: 这一小队是从较大团体中分出来的一部分，只领一项差事。

senses.title: One side in a quarrel
senses.definition: one of the opposing sides in a disagreement, especially a public or legal one
senses.definitionCN: 争执中相互对立的一方，尤指公开或法律层面的争执
senses.example: The two parties in the quarrel refused to meet.
senses.exampleCN: 争执双方都拒绝见面。
senses.why: Disagreement splits people into sides, and each side is literally a part standing against another part.
senses.whyCN: 分歧把人分成两边，每一方字面上就是与另一部分相对的一部分。

senses.title: To celebrate
senses.definition: to enjoy oneself at a celebration, often noisily and late into the night
senses.definitionCN: 在庆祝活动中尽情玩乐，常常热闹到深夜
senses.example: They partied until the neighbours complained.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一直玩到邻居来抱怨。
senses.why: The verb turns the gathering into an activity: to do what people do at a party.
senses.whyCN: 动词把「聚会」变成一种活动：做人们在聚会上会做的那些事。

senses.title: A group travelling together
senses.definition: a set of people who go somewhere together as one unit, as in a party of climbers
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个单位一起前往某处的一群人，如登山队
senses.example: A party of tourists blocked the narrow path.
senses.exampleCN: 一群游客堵住了那条窄路。
senses.why: The group is one part of all travellers, moving as a single body with a common route.
senses.whyCN: 这群人是所有出行者中的一部分，沿同一条路线作为一个整体移动。

intro.en: Party comes through Old French partie from Latin pars, partem 'part, share'. The political sense is an English extension of 'side'; the social sense later grew from 'group assembled'. The dates of both shifts are not exact.
intro.cn: 这个词经古法语中意为「部分、一方」的名词，上溯到拉丁语中意为「部分、份」的名词。政党义是英语里从「一方」引申出来的，社交义则从「聚在一起的一群人」发展而来。两次转变的具体年代都不精确。

items.en: Pars, genitive partis, meant 'part, portion, share'. It is the source of a large family: partial, particle, partner, partition.
items.cn: 这个拉丁语名词的属格词干意为「部分、份、份额」。它是庞大词族的源头，包括「部分的」「微粒」「伙伴」「分割」等词。

items.en: Partie meant 'part, portion, side', and also a division or a game. English borrowed it with the sense of a portion or a side.
items.cn: 这个古法语名词意为「部分、份、一方」，也指分割或一局游戏。英语借入时取其「一部分」或「一方」之义。

items.en: By the fourteenth century the English noun meant a part, a side, or a person taking part. The spelling settled as party later.
items.cn: 到十四世纪，英语中的这个名词已表示「一部分」「一方」或「参与者」。拼写后来才固定下来。

items.en: Party could then mean a faction or a side in a public quarrel. The step from 'faction' to 'lasting electoral organization' is generally dated to the eighteenth century but is not certain.
items.cn: 这时它已可指派系或公开争执中的一方。从「派系」到「持久的选举组织」这一步，一般认为发生在十八世纪，但并不能确定。

items.en: The 'social gathering' sense appears in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. It is generally explained as a natural extension of 'a group of people', though the exact date is imprecise.
items.cn: 「社交聚会」这一义项出现在十八至十九世纪，一般认为是从「聚在一起的一群人」这一义直接引申，具体年代不精确。

items.en: In modern usage party covers politics, law, travel and entertainment at once, which is why the single word needs context.
items.cn: 在现代用法里，这个词同时覆盖政治、法律、出行与娱乐，因此单独出现时必须靠语境判断。

note.en: The first group shares the spelling stem or the Latin source; the second group gathers words for gatherings, sides and subgroups.
note.cn: 第一组共享拼写词干或拉丁来源；第二组汇集了表示聚会、一方与小团体的词。

entries.definition: A portion, a piece or a role. It shares the Latin source but never names an organized group of people.
entries.definitionCN: 指一部分、一个零件或一个角色。它与本词同出拉丁来源，却从不表示人的组织。

entries.definition: Incomplete, or favouring one side. It is the adjective built on the same 'part' idea, not a noun for a group.
entries.definitionCN: 指不完整的，或偏袒一方的。它是同一「部分」概念构成的形容词，不是指团体的名词。

entries.definition: A firm supporter of one side, often one who refuses to hear the other. It describes a follower, not the organization.
entries.definitionCN: 指某一方的坚定支持者，往往拒听另一方。它描述跟随者，而不是组织。

entries.definition: A very small piece of matter or of language. It comes from a Latin diminutive of 'part' and has no social meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 指物质或语言中极小的单位，来自拉丁语「部分」的指小形式，没有任何社交含义。

entries.definition: Any bringing of people together. It need not be a celebration and carries no hint of music or drink.
entries.definitionCN: 指人们聚到一起的任何场合，不一定是庆祝，也不带音乐或酒水的意味。

entries.definition: An event held to mark a success or a date. It stresses the reason for meeting rather than the meeting itself.
entries.definitionCN: 为纪念某项成功或某个日子而举行的活动。它强调聚会的理由，而不是聚会本身。

entries.definition: A small group inside a larger one, often pushing its own interest. It is narrower and usually more divisive than a party.
entries.definitionCN: 较大团体内部的小团体，常推行自身利益。它比政党更窄，也通常更具分裂性。

entries.definition: One of two or more positions in a dispute. It can be a party's standpoint without being an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 指争执中的两个或多个立场之一。它可以是某一方的立场，却不构成组织。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin word for 'part', the real derived family, and the fixed phrases that keep the senses apart.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中意为「部分」的词、真实的派生词族，以及把各义项区分开的固定搭配。

normal.en: A party is a part of the people: one slice of the crowd organized to act as a whole.
normal.cn: 政党就是人的一部分：人群中的一片组织起来，像整体一样行动。

normal.en: The legal sense keeps the same picture: a contract has sides, and each side is a part.
normal.cn: 法律义保留同一幅图：合同有若干边，每一边就是一部分。

normal.en: A search party is a part cut off from the main body and sent on one errand.
normal.cn: 搜索队就是从主体上分出去、只领一项差事的一部分。

normal.en: The family runs partner, partnership, partisan, partly and partygoer.
normal.cn: 同族词包括伙伴、合伙关系、党派支持者、部分地与聚会参加者。

normal.en: Fixed phrases separate the senses: throw a party, a party to the dispute, the ruling party.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把义项分开：举办聚会、争端一方、执政党。

abstract.en: Picture a cake cut into slices: one slice is taken out, given a name and made to speak for the cake.
abstract.cn: 想象一个蛋糕被切成若干块：其中一块被取出来、起了名字，还让它代表整个蛋糕说话。

abstract.en: Every sense of the word keeps that slice: a slice of citizens, of guests, of a contract, of a crowd.
abstract.cn: 这个词的每个义项都保留着那一块：公民的一块、客人的一块、合同的一块、人群的一块。

abstract.en: So a party is always both less than the whole and loud enough to be mistaken for it.
abstract.cn: 所以一方永远既小于整体，又响得足以被误当成整体。

examples.en: The party has promised to cut the tax on fuel.
examples.cn: 这个政党承诺削减燃料税。

examples.en: He arrived at the party with a bottle of wine and no gift.
examples.cn: 他带了一瓶酒、没带礼物就来了聚会。

examples.en: Neither party may cancel the lease without two months' notice.
examples.cn: 任何一方都不得在未提前两个月通知的情况下取消租约。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「帕提」——把「怕」生冷场的人「提」到一起，再摆上吃喝，就是一场聚会；人一分派，又成了政党

root: 本词经古法语中意为「部分、一方」的名词，上溯到拉丁语 pars/partem（部分、份），本义「一部分、一方」；政党义由「一方」引申，聚会义由「聚在一起的一群人」引申。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all keep the idea of a part: a part of the citizens, a part of the guests, a part of a contract, a part of a crowd, and finally the act of enjoying the gathering.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留「一部分」的意思：公民的一部分、客人的一部分、合同的一部分、人群的一部分，最后还有享受这场聚会的行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: take one part out of a whole, give it a name, and let it act as a unit.
core.cn: 核心意象：从整体中取出一部分，给它一个名字，让它作为一个单位行动。

branches.en: NAMED GROUP AND TRAVELLING GROUP: both take one part of a larger crowd and move or speak as a single body.
branches.cn: 有名号的团体与同行的团体：两者都从更大的人群中取出一部分，作为一个整体行动或发言。

branches.en: EVENT AND VERB: the gathering is a thing, and celebrating is what people do inside it.
branches.cn: 场合与动词：聚会是一件事物，庆祝则是人们在其中做的事。

branches.en: BOUND SIDE AND ACTIVE PARTICIPANT: a contract binds a side, while a discussion welcomes a participant.
branches.cn: 受约束的一方与主动的参与人：合同约束一方，讨论则欢迎参与人。

branches.en: DETACHED CREW: a small part is cut off from the main body and sent on one job.
branches.cn: 分出来的小队：一小部分从主体上分出去，被派去完成一项任务。

branches.en: OPPOSING SIDE: disagreement splits the whole into two parts that face each other.
branches.cn: 对立的一方：分歧把整体劈成相对而立的两部分。

intro.en: Party is a Latin root plus a French noun suffix, and the same root builds a large English family.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个拉丁词根加一个法语名词后缀构成的，同一词根还构成了一大批英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pars, partem 'part' supplies the root; the noun suffix came through Old French -ie from Latin -ia.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中意为「部分」的名词提供词根；名词后缀经古法语进入英语，再上溯到拉丁语的名词后缀。

items.example: She read the first part of the report.
items.exampleCN: 她读了报告的第一部分。

items.structure: part + -y (noun suffix through Old French -ie, from Latin -ia)
items.meaningCN: 表示状态或集合体，语义偏移为「一方、团体」
items.example: The suffix turns the root into a countable noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把词根变成一个可数名词。

items.meaningCN: 只涉及一部分的，语义偏移为「不完整的、偏袒的」
items.example: A partial answer is better than none.
items.exampleCN: 不完整的答案也胜过没有答案。

items.meaningCN: 分享者，语义偏移为「伙伴、合伙人」
合伙状态，语义偏移为「伙伴关系、合伙企业」
items.example: The two doctors formed a partnership.
items.exampleCN: 两位医生结成了合伙关系。

items.structure: part- + -isan (adherent suffix via French and Italian)
items.meaningCN: 某一方的跟随者，语义偏移为「党徒、偏袒的」
items.exampleCN: 广场上到处是党派口号。

items.meaning: to take a share of something
items.meaningCN: 取一份，语义偏移为「参与、分享」
items.example: Everyone may partake of the meal.
items.exampleCN: 每个人都可以享用这顿饭。

definition_zh: 经过；通过；传递；通行证
definition_en: to go past, to pass a test, to hand over, or a card that lets you in

scene: 校门口孩子把球传给同伴，另一只手举着通行证。Please pass me the salt.

路人

senses.title: To go past something
senses.definition: To go past something
senses.definitionCN: 从旁走过
senses.example: Cars pass our house all day.
senses.exampleCN: 车辆整天经过我家。
senses.why: From Latin passus, a step.
senses.whyCN: 源自 passus（一步）。

senses.title: To pass a test
senses.definition: To pass a test
senses.definitionCN: 考试及格

definition_zh: 一段文字；通道；过道；航程；通过
definition_en: a short section of a text or a piece of music, a narrow way through or along something, a journey by sea or air, or the process of a law being approved
core_image: 一条窄廊从两堵石墙之间穿过，尽头透出一线光
scene: 老城的巷子窄得只容一人通过，石墙上还留着旧日的门框。A narrow passage led from the street into a quiet courtyard.
sceneCN: 这里的 passage 是「通道、过道」（第 2 个义项：穿过建筑或墙壁的窄路）；句意为一条窄通道从街道通向安静的院子。图中可辨识物件：石墙、门框、巷口的光。

pos.zh: 一段文字；通道；过道；航程；通过

由 pass 加 -er 与 by 复合而成，义为「路过的人；行人」

senses.title: A short section of a text or a piece of music
senses.definition: a short part of a book, poem, speech or piece of music, considered on its own
senses.definitionCN: 书、诗、演讲或乐曲中单独拿出来看的一小部分
senses.example: She read the passage aloud to the class.
senses.exampleCN: 她把这一段朗读给全班听。
senses.why: Passage first meant the act of going through, so a stretch of writing is pictured as a stretch of road that a reader travels from one end to the other.
senses.whyCN: passage 最早指「穿过去」这个动作，所以一段文字被想成一段路，读者从这头走到那头。

senses.title: A narrow way through or along something
senses.definition: a narrow way that lets a person move through a building, between walls or along a corridor
senses.definitionCN: 让人穿过建筑、墙与墙之间或沿走廊行走的窄路
senses.example: A narrow passage led from the street into a quiet courtyard.
senses.exampleCN: 一条窄通道从街道通向安静的院子。
senses.why: The word names the act of passing, and the place that makes passing possible borrows the same name: a passage is where the going-through happens.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本指「通过」这个动作，而让通过成为可能的那段空间就借用了同一个名字：passage 就是「穿过去」发生的地方。

senses.title: A journey, especially by sea or air
senses.definition: a journey from one place to another, especially by ship, and also the fare paid for it
senses.definitionCN: 从一地到另一地的行程，尤指乘船，也指为此支付的船费
senses.example: The storm made the passage across the channel dangerous.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴使横渡海峡的航程变得危险。
senses.why: A voyage is simply a long act of passing from one shore to another, so the noun for going through extends to the whole crossing and to the money it costs.
senses.whyCN: 一次航行不过是从一片岸到另一片岸的漫长「穿过」，于是表示穿过的名词扩展到整段渡海行程，以及为它付出的钱。

senses.title: The process of a law being approved, or of time going by
senses.definition: the formal approval of a law by a legislature, or the movement of time from one moment to the next
senses.definitionCN: 立法机构对法律的正式通过，或时间从一刻走向下一刻
senses.example: The passage of the new law took almost a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这项新法几乎花了一年才通过。
senses.why: A bill must go through a series of stages before it becomes law, and time goes through the hours in the same way, so both are described with the noun of passing.
senses.whyCN: 一项法案必须走过一连串阶段才能成为法律，时间也同样一小时一小时地走过去，所以两者都用这个表示「通过」的名词。

intro.en: Passage goes back to Latin passus, a step, and the verb passare, to walk or cross, which French turned into passer and then into the noun passage.
intro.cn: passage 上溯拉丁语 passus（一步）与动词 passare（走、穿过），法语把它变成 passer，又造出名词 passage。

items.en: Pandere meant to spread or stretch out, and a leg stretched forward gives the family its first picture of movement.
items.cn: pandere 意为展开、伸开，一条腿向前伸出，给了这一族词最初的移动画面。

items.en: Passus named a single step and also a fixed length of ground measured in steps.
items.cn: passus 指单独的一步，也指以步为单位量出的固定长度。

items.en: The everyday verb passare meant to walk, to cross or to go through, and it is the source of the French verb.
items.cn: 通俗拉丁语的动词 passare 意为走、越过、穿过，是法语动词的来源。

items.en: Old French made the noun passage for a crossing, a way through and a section of a text.
items.cn: 古法语造出名词 passage，指渡海、穿行的路，以及文本中的一段。

items.en: English borrowed passage in the thirteenth century and kept all three strands: the act of going through, the way itself, and a stretch of writing.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 passage，并保留了三条线索：通过的动作、通过的路，以及一段文字。

normalIntro.en: Passage keeps the picture of a step forward, and every sense is something a step can do: cross a room, cross a sea, cross a page, or carry a law to its end.
normalIntro.cn: passage 始终保留「向前一步」的画面，每个义项都是步子能做的事：穿过房间、穿过海面、穿过书页，或者把一项法案走到终点。

normal.en: Passage is pass plus the French ending -age, so the word says the act of passing before it says any place or text.
normal.cn: passage 是 pass 加法语词尾 -age，所以这个词先说的是「通过」这个动作，其次才是某处地方或某段文字。

normal.en: A passage in a building and a passage in a book share the idea of a stretch you travel along from one end to the other.
normal.cn: 建筑里的通道与书里的一段共享同一个想法：一段可以从头走到尾的路程。

normal.en: The passage of time and the passage of a bill both describe something moving through stages until it arrives.
normal.cn: 时间的流逝与法案的通过，都描述某物穿过一个个阶段，直到抵达终点。

normal.en: Passage is not the same as passenger: the first is the way or the trip, the second is the person carried along it.
normal.cn: passage 与 passenger 不同：前者是路或行程，后者是被带着走完这段路的人。

normal.en: Passion looks almost identical but comes from a Latin word for suffering, so the shared spelling is a coincidence of history.
normal.cn: passion 看起来几乎一样，却来自拉丁语中表示「受苦」的词，所以相同的拼写只是历史造成的巧合。

abstract.en: A single word for a corridor, a sea trip and a paragraph tells us that reading is also a kind of travel.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时指走廊、海上行程与段落，说明阅读本身也是一种旅行。

abstract.en: A law passes the way a person passes a gate: it must be let through stage by stage, and each stage can stop it.
abstract.cn: 法律通过就像人过一道门：必须一关一关被放行，而每一关都可能把它拦下。

abstract.en: The passage of time is the one journey nobody can refuse, which is why the word sounds calm even when it describes loss.
abstract.cn: 时间的流逝是无人能拒绝的一段行程，所以这个词即使在说失去时，听上去也很平静。

definition_zh: 乘客；旅客；随行者；旅鸽
definition_en: a person who travels in a vehicle but is not driving or working on it, a person who takes no active part in something, or the extinct migratory pigeon of North America
core_image: 渡轮甲板上挤满拎着行李的人，海风把衣角吹得鼓起
scene: 清晨的渡轮刚离岸，甲板上的人扶着栏杆看城市退远。Every passenger on the ferry watched the harbour shrink behind them.
sceneCN: 这里的 passenger 是「乘客、旅客」（第 1 个义项：乘坐交通工具的人）；句意为渡轮上的每位乘客都看着港口在身后缩小。图中可辨识物件：栏杆、行李、海面。

derivatives.zh: 与 passenger 同出古法语 passager（过往的），后受 passage 影响改写词形，义为「航程；一段文字」
这一族词的基础动词，来自拉丁语 passus（一步），义为「经过；通过」
由 passenger 与 mile 复合而成，是运输业统计客运量的单位「客英里」

senses.title: A person travelling in a vehicle
senses.definition: a person who is travelling in a car, bus, train, ship or plane and is not the one operating it
senses.definitionCN: 乘坐汽车、公共汽车、火车、轮船或飞机，但不负责驾驶的人
senses.example: Every passenger on the ferry watched the harbour shrink behind them.
senses.exampleCN: 渡轮上的每位乘客都看着港口在身后缩小。
senses.why: The word began as the adjective passager, meaning passing or fleeting, and then named the person who makes a passage; a traveller carried by someone else is exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是形容词 passager，意为「过往的、短暂的」，随后用来指走完一段行程的人；被人带着走的旅人正是这个意思。

senses.title: Someone who takes no active part
senses.definition: a person who is carried along by others and takes no active part or responsibility in what is happening
senses.definitionCN: 被别人带着走、对正在发生的事既不参与也不负责的人
senses.example: He felt like a passenger in his own company, watching others make every decision.
senses.exampleCN: 他觉得自己在自己公司里只是个随行者，看着别人做所有决定。
senses.why: Since a passenger is the one who sits still while another drives, the word easily shifts from a seat on a bus to a seat in a meeting where someone else steers.
senses.whyCN: 乘客就是别人开车时坐着不动的那个人，所以这个词很容易从公交车上的座位，挪到由别人掌舵的会议里的座位。

senses.title: The extinct North American migratory pigeon
senses.definition: a gregarious pigeon of North America that migrated in huge flocks and became extinct in the early twentieth century
senses.definitionCN: 一种成群迁徙的北美鸽子，在二十世纪初灭绝
senses.example: The passenger pigeon once darkened the sky in flocks of millions.
senses.exampleCN: 旅鸽曾以数百万只成群飞过，把天空都遮暗了。
senses.why: The bird was named for its habit of passing through in vast migrating flocks, so the same idea of passing travellers gave the species its English name.
senses.whyCN: 这种鸟因成百万只迁徙过境而得名，于是「过往的旅人」这同一个想法，给了这个物种它的英文名。

intro.en: Passenger derives from Old French passager, a traveller and also an adjective meaning passing, and its modern spelling was reshaped under the influence of passage.
intro.cn: passenger 源自古法语 passager，既指旅人，也是意为「过往的」的形容词；现代拼写是在 passage 的影响下改成这样的。

items.en: Passus, a step, and the verb passare, to cross, stand at the head of the family.
items.cn: passus（一步）与动词 passare（穿过）位于这一族词的最上游。

items.en: Old French passager meant both a traveller and something passing or brief.
items.cn: 古法语 passager 既指旅人，也指过往的、短暂的事物。

items.en: English took the word as passager, a person who makes a passage or a journey.
items.cn: 英语把它收作 passager，指走完一段行程或旅程的人。

items.en: The spelling gained an n, probably by association with passage, and became passenger.
items.cn: 拼写多出一个 n，可能是因为受了 passage 的类推，于是写成 passenger。

items.en: Modern English adds the figurative sense of a person who takes no part, and keeps the name of the extinct passenger pigeon.
items.cn: 现代英语加上「不参与其中的人」这一比喻义，并保留了已灭绝的旅鸽之名。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on pass or merely spelled alike; the near-meaning group collects words for people who travel.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在 pass 之上或只是拼写相近的词；近义组收表示出行者的词。

entries.definition: To go past something, or a permit to travel.
entries.definitionCN: 经过某物，或通行证。

entries.definition: A way through, a journey, or a part of a text.
entries.definitionCN: 通道、航程，或文本的一段。

entries.definition: An official document that lets you travel abroad; the second element is port, not a form of pass.
entries.definitionCN: 准许出国的官方证件；后半部分是 port，并非 pass 的变形。

entries.definition: A very strong feeling or enthusiasm; only the spelling is close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的情感或爱好；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A person who is making a journey.
entries.definitionCN: 正在旅行的人。

entries.definition: A person who travels regularly between home and work.
entries.definitionCN: 定期往返于家与工作地点之间的人。

entries.definition: A person who travels on a horse, bicycle or bus.
entries.definitionCN: 骑马、骑车或乘车的人。

entries.definition: A paying passenger, or the money paid for a journey.
entries.definitionCN: 付钱的乘客，或所付的车费。

normalIntro.en: Passenger is a traveller word that has been reshaped by the word for the trip, so its hooks follow the person being carried rather than the driving.
normalIntro.cn: passenger 是一个表示旅人的词，被「行程」这个词改过形，所以记忆钩子跟着「被带着走的人」，而不是开车的人。

normal.en: Passenger comes from Old French passager, a traveller, and the extra n came later under the influence of passage.
normal.cn: passenger 来自古法语 passager（旅人），多出来的 n 是后来受 passage 影响才加上的。

normal.en: The opposite of a passenger is the driver: one is carried, the other does the carrying.
normal.cn: 乘客的对立面是司机：一个被带着走，一个负责带人走。

normal.en: Passenger seat is the seat beside the driver, named from the person who usually sits there.
normal.cn: passenger seat 是司机旁边的座位，因常坐在那里的人而得名。

normal.en: The passenger pigeon was named for passing through in huge migrating flocks, not for carrying anyone.
normal.cn: 旅鸽因成百万只迁徙过境而得名，并不是因为它载过谁。

normal.en: Passport looks related but its second half is port, a harbour, so the two words only share a beginning.
normal.cn: passport 看起来相关，但它的后半部分是 port（港口），两个词只是开头相同。

abstract.en: A passenger is proof that progress is often made by someone else, which is why the word can sound grateful or helpless.
abstract.cn: 乘客的存在说明前进常常是别人完成的，所以这个词听起来既可能带着感激，也可能带着无力。

abstract.en: Being called a passenger in your own life is a quiet complaint: the vehicle moves, but your hands are not on the wheel.
abstract.cn: 在自己的人生里被叫作乘客，是一句安静的抱怨：车在走，但方向盘不在你手上。

abstract.en: A bird named after passing shows that a whole species can be remembered by one habit of movement.
abstract.cn: 一种因「过境」而得名的鸟说明：整个物种可以被一个移动的习惯记住。

examples.en: Every passenger on the ferry watched the harbour shrink behind them.
examples.cn: 渡轮上的每位乘客都看着港口在身后缩小。

examples.en: He felt like a passenger in his own company, watching others make every decision.
examples.cn: 他觉得自己在自己公司里只是个随行者，看着别人做所有决定。

examples.en: The passenger pigeon once darkened the sky in flocks of millions.
examples.cn: 旅鸽曾以数百万只成群飞过，把天空都遮暗了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派森杰」——派森杰拎着箱子挤上渡轮，找到座位就交给船夫去开；记住 passenger 是乘客。

root: 来自古法语 passager（旅人，也指「过往的」），其词根为拉丁语 passus（一步）与 passare（穿过）；现代拼写受 passage 影响加入 n，并非另有一个新词根。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a person carried along by someone else's movement; the senses divide into the traveller, the figure who takes no part, and the bird that passes in flocks.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被别人的移动带着走的人；义项按「旅人」「不参与其中的人」「成群过境的鸟」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ferry deck crowded with people holding luggage, the wind filling their coats.
core.cn: 核心意象：渡轮甲板上挤满拎着行李的人，海风把衣角吹得鼓起。

branches.en: a deck crowded with coats and bags
branches.cn: 挤满外套与行李的甲板

branches.en: a ticket checked at the gangway
branches.cn: 在舷梯口被查验的一张票

branches.en: a meeting where one person only listens
branches.cn: 一个人只带耳朵的一场会议

branches.en: a car moving while the hands stay still
branches.cn: 双手不动而车在前进

branches.en: a sky darkened by a migrating flock
branches.cn: 被迁徙鸟群遮暗的天空

intro.en: The word is a French traveller noun built on the Latin step, reshaped by the noun for the crossing, so its parts still say a person on a journey.
intro.cn: 这个词是建立在拉丁语「一步」之上的法语旅人名词，又被表示「渡海」的名词改过形，各部分至今仍在说「在旅途中的人」。

latinIntro.en: Latin passus and passare are recorded, and the French forms descend from them, so the ancestry is reliable up to the spelling change.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 passus 与 passare 均有记录，法语形式由它们而来，因此直到拼写变化之前，世系都是可靠的。

items.meaning: a person carried in a vehicle

items.meaningCN: 护照；后半为 port（港口），与 passenger 只是开头相同

definition_zh: 护照；通行证；途径
definition_en: an official document that identifies you and lets you travel abroad; also a permit to pass through a place, or something that opens the way to an opportunity
core_image: 一本深色封面的小册子递进窗口，换来一次放行
scene: 机场的查验台前排着长队，旅客把证件从包里拿出来，等着印章落下。She handed her passport to the officer and waited for the stamp.
sceneCN: 这里是「护照」（第 1 个义项：出入国境时证明身份的官方证件）；句意是她把护照递给工作人员，等对方盖章放行。画面里可想到查验台、行李牌与印章。

derivatives.zh: 由 passport 与 control 复合而成，指边境对护照的查验环节
由 passport 与 photo 复合而成，指用于护照的证件照
由 passport 与表示「持有者」的 holder 复合而成，指护照持有人

senses.title: An official document for travelling abroad
senses.definition: an official document issued by a government that identifies you and allows you to travel to other countries
senses.definitionCN: 由政府签发、证明身份并允许你前往他国旅行的官方证件
senses.example: My passport expires next spring.
senses.exampleCN: 我的护照明年春天到期。
senses.why: The word joins passing and a port: the paper that once let a traveller through a harbour gate became the paper that lets a person cross a border.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把「通过」与「港口」拼在一起：最初让旅客通过港口关卡的文书，后来成了让人跨越国境的证件。

senses.title: A permit to pass through a place
senses.titleCN: 通行证；通过某地的许可
senses.definition: an official paper allowing a person or a ship to enter, leave or move through a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 准许某人或某船进出、通过某地的官方文书
senses.example: In the old harbour, no ship sailed without a passport from the governor.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧时的港口，没有总督签发的通行证，任何船都不能出海。
senses.why: Before modern borders existed, a passport was aimed at a gate or a harbour rather than at a country, and history books still use the word that way.
senses.whyCN: 在现代国界形成之前，passport 针对的是一道关口或一个港口，而不是整个国家，历史叙述里至今保留这层用法。

senses.title: A means of reaching something
senses.definition: something that makes it possible for you to go somewhere or to achieve something
senses.definitionCN: 使你得以进入某地或取得某种成就的东西
senses.example: A good command of English is a passport to better jobs.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的英语能力是获得更好工作的敲门砖。
senses.why: If a passport opens a border, then any paper, skill or contact that opens a door can borrow the name, because the movement from document to opportunity is the same.
senses.whyCN: 既然护照能打开国界，那么任何能打开一道门的证书、技能或人脉都可以借用这个称呼，因为「从证件到机会」的这一步是相同的。

intro.en: Passport fuses a verb of stepping with the Latin word for a harbour, and the paper it names has kept that gate-opening picture for six centuries.
intro.cn: passport 把表示「迈步」的动词与拉丁语里的「港口」合在一起，这个证件名称也因此把「打开关口」的画面保留了六百多年。

items.en: Passus was a step or a pace, naming the ground a foot could cover in one stride.
items.cn: passus 意为一步、一步的距离，指一只脚迈一次所跨过的地面。

items.en: The verb passare grew from that noun and meant to step, to go through or to go by.
items.cn: 动词 passare 由这个名词发展而来，意为迈步、穿过、从旁经过。

items.en: Old French passer carried the verb into everyday speech, and a compound of passer with port named a paper for passing a port.
items.cn: 古法语 passer 把这个动词带入日常语言，passer 与 port 组成的复合词则指准许通过港口的文书。

items.en: Medieval Italian passaporto recorded the same compound for a document that let a ship or a person leave a port, and French passed the form on to English.
items.cn: 中古意大利语 passaporto 记录了同样的复合词，指让船只或人员离开港口的文书，法语又把这一形式传给了英语。

items.en: Modern English keeps the travel document as the main sense and extends the word to anything that opens a way, from a skill to a good name.
items.cn: 现代英语以出入境证件为主要义项，并把词义扩展到任何能打开通路的东西，从一门技能到好名声。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the stepping verb or on the harbour noun; the near-meaning group collects papers that grant entry or permission.
note.cn: 形近组收的是建立在「迈步」动词或「港口」名词上的词；近义组收的是准许入境或授予许可的证件。

entries.definition: To go past a point, or to hand something to someone.
entries.definitionCN: 经过某一点；也指把东西递给别人。

entries.definition: A way through, or a section of a text or a journey.
entries.definitionCN: 通道；也指文章的一段或旅程的一段。

entries.definition: A person who happens to be walking past.
entries.definitionCN: 恰好从旁边走过的路人。

entries.definition: Out of date; no longer fashionable.
entries.definitionCN: 过时的；不再时髦的。

entries.definition: An official mark or sticker in a passport allowing entry to a country.
entries.definitionCN: 护照上准许进入某国的官方签注或贴纸。

entries.definition: An official document giving permission to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 准许做某事的官方文件。

entries.definition: A paper or file that records information and can prove identity.
entries.definitionCN: 记录信息、可用以证明身份的纸张或文件。

normalIntro.en: The word is a small machine of two parts: a verb for stepping and a noun for a harbour, locked together into one paper.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由两部分咬合成一台小机器：一个表示迈步的动词，一个表示港口的名词，合成同一张纸。

normal.en: Pass means to go by, and port means a harbour, so a passport is literally a paper for going through a port.
normal.cn: pass 意为经过，port 意为港口，所以 passport 字面上就是「通过港口的纸」。

normal.en: Airports still keep the old picture alive: passport control stands exactly where a gate would be.
normal.cn: 机场仍在延续这个旧画面：护照查验处就设在相当于关口的位置。

normal.en: The plural is regular, passports, because it is an ordinary countable noun.
normal.cn: 复数按规则加 s 写作 passports，因为它就是普通的可数名词。

normal.en: The phrase a passport to success shows how a document for borders turned into a word for opportunity.
normal.cn: a passport to success 这个说法显示出：一张管边界的证件如何变成了表示机会的词。

normal.en: The stress falls on the first syllable, so the two parts are spoken as one word rather than as pass and port.
normal.cn: 重音落在第一个音节，因此两个部分读起来是一个词，而不是分开的 pass 与 port。

abstract.en: A passport is a state promising, in ink and paper, that you may be let through.
abstract.cn: 护照是国家用油墨和纸张作出的承诺：你可以被放行。

abstract.en: Every border turns a small book into a key, which is why the same word can later mean any key.
abstract.cn: 每一道国界都会把一本小册子变成钥匙，所以这个词后来能指任何一把钥匙。

abstract.en: The word reminds us that permission is a thing you can hold in your hand and lose in a minute.
abstract.cn: 这个词提醒人：许可是可以握在手里、也能在一分钟内丢掉的东西。

examples.en: She showed her passport at the desk and was waved through.
examples.cn: 她在柜台出示护照，随即被示意通过。

examples.en: A second language can be a passport to work in another country.
examples.cn: 第二门语言可以成为到别国工作的途径。

examples.en: The old rule required every vessel to carry a passport from the port authority.
examples.cn: 旧时的规定要求每艘船都携带港务当局签发的通行证。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕死跑特」——出门在外最怕丢了它，还得赶紧跑；passport 就是护照。

root: 由古法语 passer（经过）与 port（港口）复合，源头可追到拉丁语 passus（一步）与 portus（港口）；本义是准许通过港口的文书。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a paper that opens a gate; the senses run from the travel document to the older harbour permit and then to any means of access.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一张能打开关口的纸；义项从出入境证件，到较早的港口通行许可，再到任何通往机会的途径。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small dark booklet handed through a window in exchange for a nod.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本深色封面的小册子递进窗口，换来一次点头放行。

branches.en: a queue at a border desk in the early morning
branches.cn: 清晨边检柜台前的一条长队

branches.en: a ship waiting for a stamped paper before it sails
branches.cn: 一条等着盖章文书才敢出海的船

branches.en: a language certificate placed on a job application
branches.cn: 一份语言证书放在求职材料上

branches.en: the same paper serving a traveller and a vessel
branches.cn: 同一张纸先后服务于旅客与船只

branches.en: a gate that opens first for a ship and later for a career
branches.cn: 先是向船只、后是向职业打开的一道门

intro.en: Two Latin pieces hold the word together: a noun for a step with its verb, and a noun for a harbour that English still uses on its own.
intro.cn: 两个拉丁成分撑起这个词：一个表示脚步的名词及其动词，一个表示港口的名词，后者英语至今单独使用。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: a paper allowing passage through a port

definition_zh: 过去；往昔；过去的；以前的；经过；超过
definition_en: the time before now; belonging to an earlier time; moving from one side of something to the other; later than or beyond a point
core_image: 身后一条已经走完的路，脚印还在，前面的路还没踩出来
scene: 老屋的墙上挂着一排褪色的照片，屋里的人坐在灯下翻看从前的日子。He rarely talks about his past, even with close friends.
sceneCN: 这里是「过去、往昔」（第 1 个义项：已经发生的时间）；句意是他很少谈起自己的过去，对亲近的朋友也一样。画面里有旧照片、台灯和翻动相册的手。

derivatives.zh: 由 past 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「已成为过去的状态」
由 past 与 due 复合而成，义为「逾期的；过期的」
由 past 与 master 复合而成，义为「老手；行家」

senses.title: The time before now
senses.definition: the time that has already happened, considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 已经发生过的全部时间，作为整体来看
senses.example: The village has changed a great deal in the past.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子在过去发生了很大变化。
senses.why: Past began as the participle of the verb meaning to go by, and what has gone by is exactly what we call the past.
senses.whyCN: past 原本是表示「走过去」的动词的分词，凡是已经走过去的，正是一段时间意义上的「过去」。

senses.title: Gone by; belonging to an earlier time
senses.definition: describing something that existed or happened before now and is no longer as it was
senses.definitionCN: 描述在此刻之前存在或发生、如今已不再是原样的东西
senses.example: She met an old friend and they talked about past summers.
senses.exampleCN: 她遇到一位老朋友，两人聊起从前的夏天。
senses.why: Once the participle describes time that has gone by, it can stand before a noun and mark that thing as belonging to the gone-by time.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个分词用来描述「已经走过去的时间」，它就能放在名词前，把那件事物标成属于那段过去的时光。

senses.title: Beyond a point in space
senses.definition: moving from one side of a place or object to the other, and ending up beyond it
senses.definitionCN: 从某地或某物的一侧移到另一侧，最后落在它的那一边
senses.example: A bus went past the school without stopping.
senses.exampleCN: 一辆公交车经过学校却没有停。
senses.why: The idea of going by turns into a preposition of place: you move along the side and leave the point behind you.
senses.whyCN: 「从旁边走过去」这个意思后来变成表示位置的介词：你沿着旁边移动，把那个点留在身后。

senses.title: Later than a stated time or beyond a limit
senses.definition: later than a particular hour, or more than a particular amount or stage
senses.definitionCN: 晚于某个时刻，或多于某个数量、越过某个阶段
senses.example: It was past midnight when the last guest left.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一位客人离开时已经过了午夜。
senses.why: If you have walked past a mark on a road, you are now beyond it; applied to hours and numbers, the same picture gives the sense of exceeding a limit.
senses.whyCN: 如果你已经走过路上的某个标记，你就到了它之外；把这一画面用到钟点和数字上，就得到「超过某个界限」的意思。

intro.en: Past is the old participle of pass, so its history is the history of walking by, worn down into a word for time that has walked away.
intro.cn: past 是 pass 旧时的分词，它的历史就是「从旁边走过」的历史，最后磨成一个指「已经走掉的时间」的词。

items.en: Passus was a step or a pace, and it named the distance a foot could cover at one stride.
items.cn: passus 意为一步、一步的距离，指一只脚迈一次所跨过的长度。

items.en: The verb passare grew from that noun and meant to step, to go through or to go by.
items.cn: 动词 passare 由这个名词发展而来，意为迈步、穿过、从旁经过。

items.en: Old French passer carried the verb into everyday use, and its past participle passé meant gone by.
items.cn: 古法语 passer 把这个动词带入日常使用，它的过去分词 passé 意为「已经过去的」。

items.en: English took past from that participle, first as a form of the verb pass and then as an adjective and a noun.
items.cn: 英语从这一分词借入 past，先作动词 pass 的一种形式，随后作形容词和名词。

items.en: Modern English adds the prepositional uses, the grammatical term past tense, and the fixed phrase in the past.
items.cn: 现代英语又添出介词的用法、语法术语「过去时」，以及固定说法 in the past。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers relatives of the verb pass, including the French borrowing that gave English its participle; the near-meaning group gathers words for earlier time.
note.cn: 形近组收的是动词 pass 的同族词，包括把分词送给英语的那个法语借词；近义组收的是表示「较早时间」的词。

entries.definition: To go by, to move beyond, or to hand something over.
entries.definitionCN: 经过；越过；也指把东西递过去。

entries.definition: A way through, or a stretch of text or music.
entries.definitionCN: 通道；也指一段文字或音乐。

entries.definition: Someone who happens to walk past a place.
entries.definitionCN: 恰好从某处走过的路人。

entries.definition: No longer in fashion; dated.
entries.definitionCN: 过时的；不再时兴的。

entries.definition: Belonging to an earlier time or to a previous state.
entries.definitionCN: 属于较早时期或先前状态的；以前的。

entries.definition: Coming before the one mentioned or the present one.
entries.definitionCN: 在提到的那一个或现在这个之前的。

entries.definition: Belonging to a time that has gone, often used of days or years.
entries.definitionCN: 属于已逝时光的，常用于 days 或 years。

normalIntro.en: The word is a participle that learned to stand alone, so every sense still carries the small movement of walking by.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词本是一个学会独立站立的分词，所以每个义项里都还带着「从旁边走过去」的小动作。

normal.en: Past is the participle of pass: time that has passed is the past.
normal.cn: past 是 pass 的分词：已经过去的时间，就是 the past。

normal.en: Walk past a shop and you leave it behind, which is why the preposition means beyond.
normal.cn: 从一家店前走过，就把它留在身后，这就是这个介词表示「越过」的原因。

normal.en: Half past ten means the hour hand has walked past the ten mark.
normal.cn: half past ten 意为时针已经走过了十点那个刻度。

normal.en: The past tense is the verb form used for what has already happened.
normal.cn: 过去时是用来表示已经发生之事的动词形式。

normal.en: As a noun it takes a regular plural, pasts, when several different pasts are compared.
normal.cn: 作名词比较几种不同的过去时，复数按规则写作 pasts。

abstract.en: The past is not a place you can visit, only a direction you have already walked.
abstract.cn: 过去不是能去的地方，只是你已经走过的一个方向。

abstract.en: English uses one small word for time gone and space passed, hinting that memory and motion share a shape.
abstract.cn: 英语用同一个小词表示逝去的时间与走过的空间，暗示记忆与移动共享同一种形状。

abstract.en: To say something is past is to say the road behind you no longer pulls at your feet.
abstract.cn: 说某件事已经过去，等于说身后那条路不再拽着你的脚。

examples.en: The past is never as simple as it looks from here.
examples.cn: 过去从来不像从这里看上去那样简单。

examples.en: We drove past the old mill on the way home.
examples.cn: 回家的路上我们开车经过了那座老磨坊。

examples.en: It is half past nine, so the shop is already open.
examples.cn: 现在九点半，商店已经开门了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕斯特」——想起过去的事有点怕；past 就是过去。

root: 由古法语 passer 的过去分词 passé 演变而来，源头是拉丁语 passus（一步）与晚期拉丁语 passare（通过）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is movement that leaves a point behind; time that has left us becomes the noun, and space left behind becomes the preposition.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把某个点留在身后」的移动；离开我们的时间成了名词，被留在身后的空间成了介词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road already walked, footprints still visible behind the walker.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条已经走完的路，脚印还在走路人的身后。

branches.en: a lamp-lit room where old photographs are turned over
branches.cn: 灯下翻看旧照片的房间

branches.en: a summer remembered by two old friends
branches.cn: 两位老朋友回忆起的某个夏天

branches.en: a bus sliding by a school gate without stopping
branches.cn: 一辆公交车驶过校门没有停

branches.en: a clock whose hands have left midnight behind
branches.cn: 指针已经把午夜留在身后的钟

branches.en: the same word marking old days and a road just walked
branches.cn: 同一个词既标出旧日，也标出刚走过的路

intro.en: The word is built from a Latin step and its verb, filtered through a French participle that English shortened.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语中表示「一步」的名词及其动词构成，经法语分词过滤，再由英语缩短而成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to go by, to move beyond
gone by; the time before now
the verb form used with have
items.meaningCN: 与 have 连用的动词形式

definition_zh: 小路；小径；路线；路径；途径；道路
definition_en: a narrow way made for walking, the route along which someone or something travels, a course of action in life, or the chain of folders that locates a file
core_image: 湿叶覆盖的一条窄土路，尽头是湖
scene: 雨后的林子里，落叶铺满一条窄窄的土路，尽头通向湖边。We followed the path down to the lake.
sceneCN: 这里的 path 是「小路、小径」（第 1 个义项：供人行走的窄道）；句意是我们沿着这条小路走到湖边。图中可辨识物件：落叶、窄土路、湖面。

pos.zh: 小路；小径；路线；路径；途径

derivatives.zh: 由 path 与 way 复合而成，义为「通道；路径」
由 path 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无路的」
由 path 与 finder 复合而成，义为「探路者；开创者」

senses.title: A narrow track for walking
senses.definition: a narrow way made for walking, especially across fields or through woods
senses.definitionCN: 供人行走的窄道，尤指穿过田野或树林的
senses.example: We followed the path down to the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 我们沿着这条小路走到湖边。
senses.why: Path in Old English named ground worn by feet, so the first sense is physical: a line that people make simply by walking it.
senses.whyCN: 古英语的 path 指被脚踩出来的地面，所以第一个义项是实体的：一条人走着走着就形成的线。

senses.title: The route from one place to another
senses.definition: the line along which someone or something moves or travels from one point to another
senses.definitionCN: 人或物从一地移动到另一地所经过的线
senses.example: The storm changed the path of the flight.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴改变了航班的航线。
senses.why: Once a track is seen from above as a line, it can belong to anything that moves, whether feet, a plane or a beam of light.
senses.whyCN: 一条小径从高处看就是一条线，于是它可以属于任何会移动的东西：脚步、飞机或一束光。

senses.title: A course of action in life
senses.definition: a way of living or acting that leads towards a particular result
senses.definitionCN: 通向某种结果的生活方式或行动方向
senses.example: She chose a path that her parents had never taken.
senses.exampleCN: 她选了一条父母从未走过的路。
senses.why: A route leads to a destination, and a career also has a direction, so the walking word is borrowed whenever a choice has a destination in view.
senses.whyCN: 路线通向目的地，人生也有方向，所以只要一个选择看得见终点，这个走路的词就会被借去使用。

senses.title: A location in a computer system
senses.definition: the set of folders that shows where a file is stored, or the route data takes through a network
senses.definitionCN: 标明文件存放位置的文件夹序列，或数据在网络中经过的路线
senses.example: Copy the file path into the search box.
senses.exampleCN: 把文件路径复制到搜索框里。
senses.why: A file sits at the end of a chain of folders, and that chain is read as a route, so the old walking word serves computing without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 一个文件位于一串文件夹的末端，而这一串被读成一条路线，于是这个古老的走路词原样服务于计算机。

intro.en: Path goes back to Old English pæþ and to a West Germanic word for a track, reconstructed as patha; its deeper origin is uncertain, and it has no reliable Latin relative.
intro.cn: path 上溯古英语 pæþ，再上溯到一个表示「小径」的西日耳曼语词，重构形式为 patha；更早的来源不确定，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: A word reconstructed as patha named a track or a worn way, and it is the common ancestor of English path and German Pfad.
items.cn: 一个重构为 patha 的词表示小径或踩出来的路，它是英语 path 与德语 Pfad 的共同祖先。

items.en: Old English wrote the word pæþ and used it for a narrow way on the ground, with the th written by a runic letter.
items.cn: 古英语把这个词写作 pæþ，用来指地面上的一条窄路，其中的 th 音用一枚卢恩字母书写。

items.en: Middle English path kept the physical track and began to be used for the course of a journey or of a life.
items.cn: 中古英语的 path 保留实体的路径，并开始用来指一段行程或一生的走向。

items.en: Writers of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries made path to success and path of duty ordinary phrases.
items.cn: 十六、十七世纪的作者让「通往成功之路」与「责任之路」成为寻常说法。

items.en: Modern English adds the computing sense, where a path lists the folders passed through to reach a file.
items.cn: 现代英语添上计算机义：path 列出到达某个文件所经过的各个文件夹。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the compounds built on path and two Greek-derived words that merely share its spelling; the near-meaning group gathers words for tracks and routes.
note.cn: 形近组展示由 path 构成的复合词，以及两个只是拼写相近的希腊语来源词；近义组收表示小径与路线的词。

entries.definition: A path, or a course that leads from one state to another.
entries.definitionCN: 小径，或由一个状态通向另一个状态的途径。

entries.definition: A narrow path made for people on foot.
entries.definitionCN: 专供步行者走的窄道。

entries.definition: A quality in art or speech that stirs pity or sadness.
entries.definitionCN: 艺术或言辞中唤起怜悯与悲伤的特质。

entries.definition: Arousing pity, or so poor as to be contemptible.
entries.definitionCN: 引起怜悯的，或差得令人轻视的。

entries.definition: A rough path or the marks left by something moving.
entries.definitionCN: 崎岖的小道，或移动之物留下的痕迹。

entries.definition: A path through wild country, often narrow and unpaved.
entries.definitionCN: 穿过荒野的小径，通常狭窄且未铺砌。

entries.definition: The way taken from a starting point to a destination.
entries.definitionCN: 从起点到终点所走的路。

entries.definition: A road, a direction, or a method of doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 道路、方向，或做某事的方法。

normalIntro.en: Path is a native English word of uncertain deeper origin, and its hooks follow a line on the ground as it becomes a route, a life choice and finally a folder chain.
normalIntro.cn: path 是英语本族词，更早的来源不确定；记忆钩子顺着地面上的一条线，看它变成路线、人生选择，最后变成一串文件夹。

normal.en: Old English pæþ is the same word in older spelling, and the th was once written with a runic letter rather than two letters.
normal.cn: 古英语 pæþ 就是同一个词的旧拼写，其中的 th 一度用卢恩字母而不是两个字母书写。

normal.en: German Pfad and English path descend from one West Germanic word, which is why they look and sound like cousins.
normal.cn: 德语 Pfad 与英语 path 同出一个西日耳曼语词，所以它们看起来、听起来都像表亲。

normal.en: Pathway and footpath add a second noun instead of changing path itself, so the base word stays visible inside them.
normal.cn: pathway 与 footpath 都是再加一个名词，而不是改变 path 本身，所以基础词在它们里面仍然看得见。

normal.en: Pathless uses -less to say that no track exists, which is the same ending as in hopeless and careless.
normal.cn: pathless 用 -less 表示没有路，和 hopeless、careless 用的是同一个词尾。

normal.en: In computing a path is still a route: folders are places, and the path gives the order in which to pass through them.
normal.cn: 在计算机里，path 仍然是路线：文件夹是一个个地点，路径给出依次穿过的顺序。

abstract.en: A path is made by repetition: one walker leaves nothing, but enough feet wear a line into the ground.
abstract.cn: 路是被重复走出来的：一个人走过不留痕迹，脚足够多就把一条线磨进地面。

abstract.en: The word means both the line and the direction, which is why a life can be said to have a path without any ground under it.
abstract.cn: 这个词既指那条线，也指方向，所以人生即使脚下没有土地，也能说有一条 path。

abstract.en: Pathos looks like path but comes from Greek suffering, a reminder that two similar shapes can carry unrelated histories.
abstract.cn: pathos 看起来像 path，却来自希腊语中「受苦」一词，提醒人两个相似的形状可能背负毫不相干的历史。

examples.en: We followed the path down to the lake.
examples.cn: 我们沿着这条小路走到湖边。

examples.en: The storm changed the path of the flight.
examples.cn: 风暴改变了航班的航线。

examples.en: Copy the file path into the search box.
examples.cn: 把文件路径复制到搜索框里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爬石」——山间小路全是石头，得一步步爬过去；记住 path 是小路，也是路径。

root: 古英语 pæþ（小路）与德语 Pfad 同出西日耳曼语重构形式 patha，更早来源不确定；没有可靠的拉丁同族词，希腊语 pathos（受苦）只是拼写相近，与此词无关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a line worn by feet; the senses divide into the narrow track, the route of anything that moves, the course of a life and the folder chain of a file.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被脚踩出来的一条线；义项按「窄窄的小径」「任何移动之物的路线」「人生的走向」「文件的文件夹链」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow soil track under wet leaves, leading to a lake.
core.cn: 核心意象：湿叶覆盖的一条窄土路，尽头是湖。

branches.en: wet leaves over a soil track
branches.cn: 湿叶盖住的土路

branches.en: a gap in a hedge made by walkers
branches.cn: 行人踩出的树篱缺口

branches.en: a flight redrawn around a storm
branches.cn: 为避开风暴而改画的航线

branches.cn: 父母都没做过的选择

branches.cn: 以单个文件结尾的文件夹链
